table: Figure 11 (review volume, post-monetization giveaways); simple aggregate printed in results/demand/demand-log.txt
replication_status: exact (did::att_gt with the authors' settings reproduces the authors' simple aggregate 15.5344 (0.2691), which equals the printed 15.53 to the printed decimals; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: Same design as F11_csa_vol_premon on post-monetization giveaway books (giveaway Jan 2018 or later) plus similar never-giveaway books (demand_data_cleaning_code.R line 314). Panel extracted from vol_postmon_attgt_similarcontrol.gz: 1,138,916 book-months, 45,862 ids (22,931 treated + 22,931 never-treated), 27 cohorts, 48 periods. Re-aggregating the shipped object reproduces 15.53444 (analytic SE 0.2618; authors' 0.2691 is bootstrap). Authors used anticipation = 1; not representable in the pipeline (deviation). AUTHORS' CSA SETTINGS (PROTOCOL 5b Hull alignment (c), Nov 2; demand_data_cleaning_code.R lines 301-376, 02_demand_results.R lines 400-457): did::att_gt(control_group = 'nevertreated', allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, est_method dr, base_period varying, anticipation = 1), aggte(type = 'simple', na.rm = TRUE). csa_control_group = 'nevertreated'. anticipation = 1 means the base period is g-2 and the anticipation month g-1 of treated books is used neither as a pre nor a post period. It is represented without a new field: data file *_panel_ant.rds (prepared copy, prep_anticipation.R in the same folder) adds g_ant = giveaway month - 1 and ant_row = treated book-month at giveaway month - 1; gvar = g_ant and sample_filter ant_row == 0. The (g_ant, g_ant) cell is then empty (dropped by aggte na.rm), the base period is g_ant - 1 = g-2 and the post cells start at the giveaway month, so the simple ATT equals the authors' (checked). The same rows are dropped for TWFE and BJS (PROTOCOL (c)); on the retained rows the TWFE indicator is 1[month >= giveaway month]. Superseded: the earlier note that anticipation = 1 is not representable. Hull default (not-yet-treated, no anticipation) on the original panel gives 11.2546. TIMING: the paper's TWFE (Table 4, spec T4vol_c2_post_giveaway) starts treatment the month AFTER the giveaway (post_giveaway = 1(yearmon > giveaway_yearmon)), whereas the CSA (gname = giveaway month) treats the giveaway month as the first treated period; this spec's constructed TWFE follows the CSA timing, so it is not comparable to the published Table 4 TWFE.
published_source: Printed in Section 4.5.1 of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.01390.pdf): 'The overall treatment effect of Giveaway participation on number of ratings is 5.75 ... and 15.53', no SE printed; read Nov 4 2026; equals the authors' simple aggregate 15.5344 (0.2691) in results/demand/demand-log.txt to the printed decimals (authors_code_*). Earlier: Article (Management Science 72(3), 2026) Section 4.5.1: 'The overall treatment effect of Giveaway participation on number of ratings is 5.75 for the pre-monetization sample, compared with 15.53 for the postmonetization sample'; Figure 11 plots the dynamic ATTs. published_coef/se (15.5344, bootstrap 0.2691) are the authors' printed simple aggregate in results/demand/demand-log.txt, which rounds to the text value.
csa_weights_note: Nov 2: the published CSA comes from R did (or staggered, whose estimates did reproduces), which weights cells by fixed cohort shares; Hull's DiD-averaging weights cells by treated-observation counts. 'did' reproduces the published number (main analysis, option B); the strict-Hull run (CSA_STRICT_HULL=1, option A) ignores this field.
